bracket: [Textbook note (not an error): the question asks for BOTH the radius and the energy of the first orbit of \(\mathrm{He^{\oplus}}\), but the book's printed working stops the radius line at the unevaluated fraction \(\dfrac{52.9 \times 1^2}{2}\) and never states a value, so as printed only half the question is answered. The expression is correct and evaluating it gives \(r_1 = 26.45\ \mathrm{pm}\), which is the missing answer. The printed line is preserved exactly as it appears. The energy part is complete and correct: \(-2.18 \times 10^{-18} \times \dfrac{2^2}{1^2} = -8.72 \times 10^{-18}\ \mathrm{J}\).]

[Textbook misprint: the stem prints the physicist's name as "Plank". It is Max **Planck**, and the quantity is Planck's constant. The chapter misspells it the same way throughout section 4.5.1, so this is the book's house spelling rather than a one-off slip in this question. The value asked for is unaffected.]

[Textbook misprint: the fourth alternative is printed as "orientation of in the orbital electron cloud", which is not a grammatical phrase — the words have evidently been transposed, and the alternative intended is the orientation of the electron cloud in the orbital, i.e. the property fixed by the magnetic quantum number \(m_l\). It is transcribed exactly as printed. The reading does not change the answer: on either reading that alternative describes orientation, which is not what the principal quantum number describes.]

[Textbook misprint: the second group is printed as \(\mathrm{Ar}\), \(\mathrm{Cl^{2-}}\), \(\mathrm{K^{\oplus}}\). Chlorine (\(Z = 17\)) forms the UNInegative chloride ion \(\mathrm{Cl^{-}}\); a dinegative \(\mathrm{Cl^{2-}}\) would carry 19 electrons and so would NOT be isoelectronic with \(\mathrm{Ar}\) and \(\mathrm{K^{\oplus}}\), which both carry 18 — evidently what the group was set up to demonstrate, and what the chapter's own sentence on page 51 ("Species such as Ar, \(\mathrm{Ca^{2\oplus}}\) containing 18 electrons are isoelectronic with \(\mathrm{K^{\oplus}}\)") describes. The stem is transcribed exactly as printed and the solution below works out both readings.]

[Textbook misprint: the stem prints "quantum numbrs" for quantum numbers. Note also that the azimuthal quantum number is set upright in this item rather than in the italic \(l\) the rest of the chapter uses, so on the printed page it is not typographically distinguishable from the digit 1; it is read here as \(l\), since "\(n = 2\), \(1 = 1\)" would name no quantity. Neither point affects the answer.]

[Textbook misprint: the book labels this item "J.", repeating the label of the item three places above it — the sequence printed on page 54 runs I, J, K, **J**, M, N, ... with no L anywhere.
